h1: Live music and entertainment licences for a brewpub in India
title: Brewpub Live Music Licences in India | Craft Beer School
desc: The permissions a brewpub in India usually needs for live bands, DJs and recorded music, how they fit together and what to check with your state.
teaser: The band is booked and the posters are up. Then someone asks whether you have the licence for the speakers.
standfirst: Music fills a brewpub on a slow Thursday. It also brings its own permissions, separate from the brewing and bar licences. Here is how the pieces usually fit together in India.
sections:
Your brewery licence lets you make beer. Your bar licence lets you serve it. Neither automatically lets you play music to a paying crowd or put a band on a stage. In most Indian cities, music and entertainment sit under a different set of permissions, handled by different offices and agencies. Founders who learn this two weeks before opening tend to learn it the expensive way.

Rules vary by state and by city. They also change. Treat what follows as a map of the usual questions, then check the current requirements with your local authorities or a licensing consultant.

Playing recorded songs in a commercial space is a public performance under copyright law. That usually needs permission from whoever controls the rights. In India this has meant licences from collecting bodies or agencies representing the sound recordings and the underlying songs. Which ones you need depends on the catalogue you play. The area has seen disputes and court cases over the years, so take current advice rather than relying on what another outlet did.

Streaming apps on a personal account generally do not cover commercial use. Background music services aimed at businesses exist and may include the licensing. Read what their terms actually cover.

Live performance can bring further requirements. Many cities ask venues to hold a licence or permission from the police or the municipal body for public entertainment or amusement, sometimes per event and sometimes per year. Ticketed events can bring extra conditions. A band playing its own songs may raise fewer copyright questions than a covers band, but the venue permission still applies.

Check whether your excise licence sets conditions on events, hours or the area where alcohol can be served during them. Some states also tie the permitted closing time to the type of licence.
Noise, neighbours and the fire officer

Noise rules in India limit sound levels by area and restrict amplified sound late at night in open spaces. Rooftop and open air brewpubs feel this first. A complaint from a residential building next door can stop the music faster than any missing licence.

Plan the room before the playlist. Acoustic treatment, a limiter on the sound system and a stage that faces away from neighbours cost less than a dispute. If an event brings a bigger crowd, your fire safety approval and occupancy limit still apply. The fire officer counts heads, not the line at the bar.
Building it into your opening plan

Add music permissions to your licence tracker alongside excise, FSSAI and the trade licence, with an owner and a renewal date for each. Our brewery compliance checklist is a good place to start that list. Budget the fees as a recurring cost, not a one-time setup expense.

Then decide what music is for. A Friday band that brings a crowd who stay for three rounds is a sound investment. A DJ that drowns out conversation on a quiet Tuesday may cost more in licences and fees than it earns. Our guide to taproom events covers how to judge which nights deserve the effort.

Put every booking in writing, even for a friend's band. A short agreement should cover the fee, set times, sound check, who supplies the sound system, what happens if the show is cancelled and who is responsible for any music licensing for the performance. Ask whether the act plays original material or covers, because that can change who needs which copyright permission. Agree food and drink for the performers in advance. Make sure nobody on stage is drinking on your tab past the point of performing well.

Keep a simple events log: date, act, licence used, crowd size and the night's sales. After a few months it tells you which nights pay for their licences and fees.

Inspections happen during service, usually on the busiest night. Keep copies of every current licence in a folder behind the bar and make sure the duty manager knows where it is. A venue that can show its paperwork in two minutes has a very different evening from one that cannot.

Licences are only one strand of running a brewpub. The founders who cope best treat them as part of the operating plan, alongside staffing, costs and pricing, rather than as a separate headache.
faqs: Do I need a licence to play Spotify in my brewpub?

Personal streaming accounts are generally not licensed for commercial use. You usually need public performance permission or a business music service. Check the current requirements with a licensing adviser.
Does a live band need a separate permission?
In many Indian cities, yes. Public entertainment permissions from the police or municipal body often apply, on top of your excise and bar licences. Rules vary by state and city.
Can my excise licence limit events?
It can. Some licences set hours, areas or conditions for events. Read your licence conditions and ask the excise office if unsure.
